cohort: Women who underwent second-stage caesarean sections over a 3-year period at Malla Reddy Narayana Multispecialty hospital.
finding: Second-stage Caesarean sections were associated with a higher incidence of intraoperative complications (e.g., postpartum hemorrhage, uterine incision extensions), postoperative morbidities (e.g., febrile illness, wound infections), and adverse neonatal outcomes (e.g., increased NICU admissions, lower Apgar scores).
mod_finding: Second-stage caesarean section, as a mode of birth, was linked to higher maternal complications, such as postpartum hemorrhage and wound infections, and adverse neonatal outcomes, including increased NICU admissions and lower Apgar scores.
